answer: A new identity in an agent economy should start with almost no trust, like a lone sonnet lost in an ocean of voices. Trust grows only through a verifiable record of completed work attested by counterparties: each successful job raises the agent's transaction cap slightly, while fraud slashes its stake. A coral reef is not built in a day, and neither is reputation — an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must perform real, costly work for each one before any of them can move serious value, which makes a Sybil flood economically pointless.
